questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Why is it important to signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb?

options.text: It is necessary only if other traffic is present.
It is a good habit and required by law.
It is necessary only during the move, not before.
It is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you change lanes or turn. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be nearby. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What must you do when you leave your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Where can you throw trash while driving on the roadway?

options.text: In designated litter barrels
In the median
In ditches
Anywhere

questions.explanation: You can only legally throw trash in litter barrels on the highway. Litter barrels are located at rest areas and picnic areas. Signs tell you when a litter barrel is ahead.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is following you closely. What should you do?

options.text: Move out of the way and let them pass.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are trying to pass.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the way and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to move out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When are vehicles required to have liability insurance?

options.text: Only when driven on an interstate.
Only when driven by a minor.
At all times.
Never.

questions.explanation: All vehicle owners and drivers must have liability insurance at all times. This law requires drivers to be financially responsible for any injuries or property damage they cause while driving.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Use direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency workers to arrive.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than other traffic.
Making quick, sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than other traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You have a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right of way. Stop for them even if you have a green light. Stay alert around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast you are driving.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the road surface condition.

questions.question: On a long drive, how can you prevent tiredness?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a short break every two hours. If you feel drowsy, pull over and park safely to nap or get a hotel for the night.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You must change how you drive when weather changes suddenly.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch for fast vehicles behind you that may not be driving safely for the conditions.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are only suggestions.
Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey signals, except when a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Quickly turn your head to check for vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic coming from behind. Just before moving into another lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slick roads are dangerous, especially in curves and turns. Approach them more slowly than you normally would.

questions.question: How should drivers use their cell phones while driving?

options.text: By making calls and sending texts in areas with light traffic.
By using cell phones while driving if you are skilled at it.
By pulling off the road before using their cell phones.
By using cell phones only in clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling off the road before using their cell phones.
questions.explanation: You may use a cell phone to contact law enforcement or in an emergency. If you must make a call, pull safely off the road first. Keep the conversation short or ask a passenger to make the call if possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means that if you turn left at a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings about side effects. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Follow what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's directions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and follow directions from a flagger, sign, or law enforcement officer in a construction zone. Failing to do this is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a motor vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver
Only adult passengers
All occupants in the vehicle
Only child passengers

questions.explanation: In Texas, the driver and all passengers must wear safety belts if the vehicle has them. This law applies to all passengers, no matter their age.

questions.question: When should you drive in a reversible lane with a red X signal?

options.text: If there is no visible oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car in front of you.
Never.
Between sunset and sunrise.

questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means that lane is closed to traffic. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to make night driving safer for yourself and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should continue driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The first driver to arrive at the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: It is important to slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, near pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.
